description: This graph creates a non-intersecting instance setup using the properties of triangles.
documentation:
## Incircle Packing

### What is it?

Incircle packing is a variation of circle packing algorithms that makes use of the mathematical properties of triangles.

The circle that is centered within a triangle and touches all side is called the **incircle**.  The center and radius of this circle can be derived from any triangle.

### What does it do?

This graph utilizes this property of triangles to produce a scatter-like result that has no interpenetration between instances.  Because the positions and radii are based off the mesh, this means that anything instanced onto those points will not overlap (depending on instance scale).  Because the derivation of the position and radius is a mathematical operation, it is very fast to calculate.

### Inputs and outputs

The main input for this graph is an adaptive triangulated surface.  This is setup and demonstrated in the `dummy_adaptive_geo` compound.  The `incircle_packing` compound takes the resulting mesh and derives the position and radius from this.

Other inputs are the instances (trees and buildings), a field controlling instance weights and an instance masking field which controls whether the instance is a tree or a building.

The graph outputs instances placed on the incircle positions - like a scatter, but without using one.

### How it works

- The `triangle_check` compound makes sure the mesh is triangulated

- Because this graph also supports component tags, this is handled before anything happens

- The mesh and indices are fed into the `get_required_triangle_data` compound.  This derives the incenter positions and incircle radius from the triangles in the mesh.  **This compound drives everything.**

- The instances are then setup according to the instance input data, including multi-instances for the trees and the instancing itself is done.  This is laid out in three sections of the graph.

- The colours and orientations are then passed to the display terminal, with a switch allowing replacing the instances with circles to test the output.

_notes.text: This compound generates the triangulated mesh of the packing, as well as the renderable, adaptive  ground plane.

# incircle packing

Incircle packing is a variation of circle packing algorithms that makes use of the mathematical properties of triangles.

The circle that is centered within a triangle and touches all side is called the **incircle**.  The center and radius of this circle can be derived from any triangle.

This graph utilizes this to produce a scatter-like result that has no interpenetration between instances.  While it does the same thing as *bluenoise_minimal* within the ***scatter_points*** compound it is very much faster.

# prepare the mesh
The mesh should be triangulated.

This compound checks to see if the mesh is triangulated, and if it isn't, uses ***triangulate_mesh*** to triangulate.

# Component Tags

Because the ***incircle_packing*** compound runs on the *face component*, this section of the graph will try to find any component tags that exist on the mesh coming in.

A custom tag is able to be connected, or all tags are detected.

If the component tags supplied don't exist or tags don't exist on the mesh, **all faces** are used.

# triangle data
This uses each triangle in the mesh to generate the center and radius of a  circle (called the incircle) which is used to control the position and size of the resulting instances.

**This compound drives the entire graph**

# Multi-instance

Because this graph uses different instances for visual pleasure and a deeper learning experience, those instances need to be defined.  

The difficulty in this case is that the "trees" instances are 4-5 different instance objects, but the "buildings" are a single instance.

This is addressed later, but this section defines the **main** split between instances and provides a boolean array of true and false, defining instance 0 and instance 1

Because the input mesh is adaptive, some of the final triangles are very small.  This compound will identify any incenter points below a threshold based on the inradius generated for each triangle.  These are used to deletea points later on

# instance selection

The ***instance_selector*** compound takes the boolean data from the instance selection field, and converts it to *point_instance_id* values.

In this case, the boolean data represents "tree" or "building" and 4 different ids are generated for the "tree" instances.

_notes.text:
# Triangles

Triangles are mathematically rich in properties, as shown in the compound above.

Only the *incenter* and *inradius*, are needed for this compound - these describe a circle that is centered within the triangle and touches all sides of the triangle.

This is good for instancing as it guarantees no intersections between instances.

_backdrops.title: Custom node for getting triangle properties
If input tags exist, use them
If detected tags requested, use them

_notes.text:
# generate some terrain

Using 2 fields, a displacement map  is generated, that includes flatten certain areas.  The field used for flattening areas is promoted to output for use in choosing different instances for the final output.

# adaptivity and extrusions

Because an extrusion is needed to achieve the adaptive by property effect, the display and render planes need to be adjusted to match the topmost plane of the extrustion.  This section drives that offset.

# adaptive triangle mesh

Incircle packing drives the size of the resulting instances from the size of the triangle's incircle.  This means that an adaptive mesh (triangles of different sizes) will produce a better looking result.

This section utilises the ***sqrt3_subdivide_mesh*** compound to generate an adaptive mesh from a property generated from the displacement - point gradient or more specifically how steep that gradient is.

# display and rendering

Instead of calculating the heavier extruded mesh used to generate the adaptive mesh.  A simple plane that matches the surface is used, displaced to match
